Split a book section into chapter files using known headings

Source: R/split_book_section_by_headings.R
split_book_section_by_headings.Rd

Splits one oversized section text file into chapter-level .txt files by finding the ordered chapter headings supplied from a table of contents. This is useful when uppercase headings alone are ambiguous because non-chapter subsections use the same visual style.

Usage

split_book_section_by_headings(
  input_file,
  chapter_titles,
  output_dir = file.path(dirname(input_file), "chapters"),
  chapter_ids = NULL,
  extension = "txt",
  overwrite = FALSE,
  include_heading = TRUE,
  allow_missing = FALSE
)

Arguments

input_file

Character scalar. Path to the section .txt file.

chapter_titles

Character vector of chapter titles, in the order they appear in input_file.

output_dir

Character scalar. Folder where chapter files should be written. Defaults to a chapters/ subfolder beside input_file.

chapter_ids

Optional character vector of file stems to use for output files. Defaults to numbered slugs based on chapter_titles.

extension

Character scalar output extension, without a leading dot. Defaults to "txt".

overwrite

Logical scalar. If TRUE, replace existing output files. Defaults to FALSE.

include_heading

Logical scalar. If TRUE, keep each chapter heading as the first line of its output file. Defaults to TRUE.

allow_missing

Logical scalar. If TRUE, missing headings are skipped with a warning. Defaults to FALSE.

Value

A tibble with one row per written chapter and columns for the chapter title, output file, source line boundaries, and word count.
